thread:
ravi: Heads up — AWS rep flagged our preemptible->regular conversion behavior during QBR. There's a weird billing line on Feb invoice. Anyone else see this? :eyes:

olivia: saw it, opened a ticket with finance. looks like conversion credits didn't apply to 2 invoices.

simon: can you paste the invoice lines? We may have auto-conversion policy that triggered when region capacity dropped. That would move spot to on-demand at higher rate.

ravi: pasted below:
```
Invoice 2026-02-12
SKU: us-west2-gpu-spot-conv
Description: Preemptible->Std conversion
Amount: $4,800.00
Expected Credit: -$4,800.00
Billed: $4,800.00
```

olivia: finance CSV shows billed charge, not credit. I'm attaching the reconciliation ticket ID: FIN-4231 (will paste CSV in thread).

aws-sales: Hi team, quick context — conversion events caused by capacity constraints can be billed as temporary on-demand until reservations cover the usage. We can review and apply off-cycle credits if the usage is within the committed scope. Please send the invoice lines + usage CSV. (cc @contracts-bot) :wave:

contracts-bot: Noted — Contract excerpt 6.2.1: "Provider may reclassify preemptible capacity as 'transitional' when region free capacity <70% for 3 consecutive days; credits apply only where Customer provides 14-day notice of planned conversion." See internal link: https://contracts.redwood/edp/latest#6.2.1

maria: that 14-day notice is new to me. Our autoscale-driven failovers aren't run through that process. We didn't file notices for these spikes.

simon: timeline: we had an unexpected regional preemption window Feb 9–11; autoscaler moved workloads and conversions happened Feb 10. We didn't plan it so no 14-day notice.

ravi: ok — negotiating point: ask for retrospective credit and ask to add a 'conversion smoothing' clause to future EDPs so conversions inside commitment count as committed usage (or at least capped).

aws-sales: commercial can offer a compromise: apply a one-time 50% off-cycle credit for these events and include a conversion smoothing cap in next-term negotiations. Full retrospective credit requires escalation. Need 6 months of usage history to quantify risk.

olivia: finance — 50% credit reduces immediate exposure but still material. We'll need to mark the remainder as disputed. Can you get the CSV and invoice exports?

contracts-bot: Suggestion: request vendor to add a daily 'conversion audit' feed (line-item export) + an explicit conversion cap (e.g., conversions can't exceed X% of committed monthly GPU spend) in the SOW. Legal prefers numeric caps.

maria: agreed. also request a clause that conversion events triggered by provider capacity shortfall are auto-classified as committed usage for billing if they occur <72 hours after a capacity alert we generated.

simon: I'll run a 6-month tail-run to estimate frequency by region and worst-case monthly conversion spend. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

ravi: perfect. target ask: full credit OR (50% credit + contractual smoothing cap at 3% of committed GPU spend monthly). Ops will supply CSV.

aws-sales: we'll standby. If you provide the CSV and the draft redline, we can escalate to the commercial lead and engineering ops on our side. We'll also surface the possibility of emitting a daily conversion log feed.

olivia: noted action items: finance reconcile FIN-4231 with CSV; if 50% is accepted,-book revenue adj.

ravi: action items recap: simon -> run tail-run CSV (due EOD tomorrow), olivia -> finance reconciliation + disputes, ravi -> draft ask and redline, maria -> add conversion feed request and proposed smoothing language.

contracts-bot: Reminder — internal turnaround for redline review ~48–72 hours once draft received.

ravi: thanks everyone. we'll review simon's numbers tomorrow and finalize the vendor ask. prepping vendor call for Friday 10:00 PT. :thumbsup:
